rq-wf-01.front: The four parts of a waterfowl day?
rq-wf-01.diagram:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 400 348" font-family="sans-serif" role="img" aria-label="Pattern bars for a fall day, 5:00 to 20:00, pattern only, 65 to 70 percent. Mallards and other dabblers often feed at night, fly at dawn to a day roost, roost and loaf through the day and fly out at dusk to feed. Canada geese roost on water, fly to fields in the morning and late afternoon and rest on water at midday, then roost. On stormy days geese fly all day, 70 percent. Dashed lines: legal duck hours at Heffley Creek on 15 October, about 6:52 to 18:41. Times shift by day and place.">

rq-wf-04.front: When do Dutch GPS mallards commute?
rq-wf-04.back: At dusk and dawn between a day roost and night feeding sites (65%).

rq-wf-05.back: Early morning and late afternoon; more all day in storms (70%).

rq-wf-07.front: Where should the wind be at your blind?
rq-wf-07.back: At your back or quartering from behind (70%).

rq-wf-08.back: Dabblers jump straight up; divers patter across the water (80%).

rq-wf-09.front: Legal hours for ducks and geese?
rq-wf-09.back: 30 minutes before sunrise to 30 minutes after sunset (99%).

rq-wf-10.front: Heffley Creek legal duck start on 15 October 2026?

rq-wf-11.front: Boat rule for ducks and geese?
rq-wf-11.back: Not from a moving boat with a motor or sail; beached or anchored is fine (99%, 95%).

rq-wf-12.back: Watch the evening flight from far away, hunt the morning.

rq-wf-13.back: No. Hunt the feed and rest the roost (Tip).
